how: She explained how the machine works in simple terms.
bicycle: a two-wheeled vehicle powered by pedaling
He rides his bicycle to work every morning to save money.
stays: continues to be in a place or condition
The lake stays frozen well into early spring.
upright: vertical; standing straight up without leaning
the: used before a noun to refer to a specific or already-known thing
The cat sat quietly on the windowsill all afternoon.
popular: liked, supported, or used by many people
That café became popular with students soon after it opened.
explanation: a statement or account that makes something clear
The popular explanation is wrong, and the real one is stranger.
is: present tense (he/she/it) of the verb be
The library is open until nine o'clock every evening.
wrong: not correct or true; not what is required
The popular explanation is wrong, and the real one is stranger.
and: used to connect words, phrases, or clauses
We packed sandwiches, fruit, and water for the long hike.
real: actually existing; genuine, not imagined or fake
The documentary tells the real story behind the famous painting.
one: Only one seat was left when we arrived at the theatre.
stranger: more unusual or surprising (comparative of strange)
The truth turned out to be stranger than anyone had guessed.
ask: to put a question to someone or request something
Feel free to ask if you need help with the homework.
most: the majority of; the greatest amount or number of
Most of the guests had already left by the time the rain started.
cyclists: The city added a protected lane to keep cyclists safe from traffic.
why: Why does the air above a city stay warm long after sunset?
does: performs an action, or auxiliary form used in questions and negatives
She does her best to help everyone around her.
not: used to make a statement, verb, or phrase negative
The results are not as clear as we had hoped.
fall: a decrease in amount, level, or value
The report records a steady fall in river fish populations.
over: during the whole of a period of time; more than
Prices have risen steadily over the past five years.
they: used to refer to people or things already mentioned, as the subject
They arrived late because of heavy traffic on the highway.
will: used to express the future tense
A fact heard once looks, from the inside, like a fact that will never be needed again.
mention: to refer to something briefly, especially in speech or writing

spinning: turning around quickly on an axis or centre point
The washing machine drum keeps spinning for several more minutes.
wheels: circular objects that turn on an axle to allow movement

it: used to refer to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
She lost her phone and later found it under the sofa.
reasonable: The landlord offered a reasonable price for the small apartment.
guess: an estimate or opinion formed without certain knowledge
My guess is that the meeting will be postponed until next week.
for: intended to belong to, or be given to, someone or something
She bought a small gift for her best friend.
long: having a great length or duration
It was a long journey across three different countries.
time: the continuous progress of existence measured in seconds, minutes, hours, etc.
Planting street trees releases water vapour and shades the ground at the same time.
was: past tense of 'be', used for the first/third person singular
Half an hour after a lesson ends, much of what was said is already gone.
standard: a level of quality or an accepted way of doing something
This factory follows a strict safety standard.
on: positioned at or touching the surface of something
She placed the keys on the table by the door.
its: belonging to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
The cat licked its paw before curling up to sleep.
own: to possess something, or belonging to oneself
Few families in the village own a car of their own.
also: The recipe also works well with chicken instead of beef.
do: to perform an action, or an auxiliary verb used in questions and negatives

resist: to refuse to accept or to fight against something

being: existing, or the fact of existing in a particular state

tipped: made to lean or fall over

an: used before a word starting with a vowel sound to mean 'one'
She ordered an apple juice and a sandwich for lunch.
effect: a change that results from an action or cause
Cutting sugar had a noticeable effect on her energy levels.
anyone: Anyone interested in the workshop should sign up before Friday.
can: used to express ability or possibility
Anyone with an internet connection can join the online course.
feel: to sense or experience something physically or emotionally
You can feel the ground shake when a train passes by.
by: indicating the agent, method, or proximity of something
The letter was written by hand and delivered by courier.
holding: gripping or supporting something with one's hands
She stood at the door, holding a bunch of flowers.
turning: moving or rotating in a circular direction
An effect anyone can feel by holding a turning wheel by its axle.
wheel: a circular object that turns on an axle to allow movement
Spinning wheels resist being tipped over, an effect anyone can feel by holding one.
axle: a rod connecting a pair of wheels
The old cart's axle creaked loudly with every turn of the wheel.
but: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been said
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving soon.
researchers: people who carry out careful study
Researchers have tracked the glacier's retreat for thirty years.
have: used with a past participle to form perfect tenses
They have finished the report ahead of schedule.
built: constructed, past tense and participle of build
The bridge was built over a hundred years ago and still stands today.
bicycles: The city built new lanes so bicycles could travel safely downtown.
with: Neighbourhoods with few trees heat up fastest, and these are often the poorest districts.
that: used to identify a specific thing, person, or clause already mentioned
The book that you gave me last year is still on my shelf.
cancelled: neutralized or made to have no effect

out: away from the inside of a place; not in
She stepped out for a few minutes to get some fresh air.
second: coming after the first in order

backwards: in the direction of the back; in reverse

removes: This filter removes fine dust from the air effectively.
machines: devices with moving parts that perform tasks
Modern washing machines use far less water than older models.
still: continuing to be the case; even more so
Despite the rain, the match still went ahead as planned.
balanced: kept steady, with different parts equal or in proportion

perfectly: in a perfect manner; completely or entirely

well: in a good or satisfactory way

what: used to ask for information about something
The reason lies in what cities are actually made of.
actually: in fact; really, contrary to what might be expected
The film was actually shot in a different country than the story suggests.
keeps: continues to have, hold, or maintain something (he/she/it)
Regular exercise keeps the body strong and flexible.
steering: the act or system of controlling the direction of a vehicle
The car's steering felt loose after the accident.
when: The baker's skill lies in knowing when to wait and when to stop waiting.
frame: the rigid structure that supports and shapes something
The bicycle frame was made of lightweight aluminium.
begins: The film begins with a dramatic scene in the mountains.
to: expressing direction, purpose, or a recipient
The sun has set, the traffic has thinned, and yet the air refuses to cool.
lean: to bend or slope in a particular direction
She had to lean forward to hear the quiet announcement.
left: remaining after others have gone or been used
Only a few seats were left by the time we arrived.
front: the part of something that faces forward or is seen first
She parked the car right at the front of the building.
turns: present tense of turn, used with he/she/it; changes direction
When the frame begins to lean to the left, the front wheel turns slightly to the left as well.
slightly: to a small degree; a little
The room felt slightly colder after the window was opened.
as: used to compare, or to mean 'while' or 'because'
As the sun set, the temperature dropped quickly.
turn: a change of direction; a movement of rotation
That turn moves the wheels back underneath the falling weight, and the bicycle straightens.
moves: A skilled cyclist moves the handlebars only slightly to stay balanced.
back: returning to a previous place, position or condition
She promised to call him back as soon as she landed.
underneath: in a position below something else
That turn moves the wheels back underneath the falling weight, and the bicycle straightens.
falling: She watched the falling leaves drift across the yard.
weight: how heavy something is; a heavy object
That turn moves the wheels back underneath the falling weight of the rider.
straightens: The mechanism straightens itself once the weight is removed.
process: a series of actions taken to achieve a result
Learning a new language is a slow and gradual process.
repeats: happens again in the same way
The chorus repeats three times before the song ends.
several: more than two but not very many
Several guests arrived late because of the traffic.
times: plural of time; particular occasions or periods
This is why recipes that give exact times are unreliable.
far: to a great extent; at or to a great distance
This plan works far better than the last one did.
faster: moving or acting more quickly; comparative of fast
The new engine makes the car noticeably faster.
than: used to introduce the second part of a comparison
This year's harvest was larger than last year's.
rider: a person who travels on a bicycle, motorbike, or animal
The rider adjusted her balance as the road turned sharply.
think: to use the mind to consider something or form an opinion
I need some time to think before I answer you.
about: The lecture was about how cities cope with extreme heat.
part: a piece or portion of a whole
Only a small part of the report dealt with financial risks.
of: used to show belonging, origin, or a relationship between two things
The cover of the book was torn at the corner.
comes: moves toward or arrives at a place; originates from
Fresh bread comes out of the oven every morning at six.
from: indicating the point where something starts or originates
The letter came from a friend living overseas.
design: a plan or drawing showing how something will be made
The new phone's design won several awards for innovation.
itself: used to refer back to a thing or situation already mentioned, for emphasis
The machine can clean itself without any help from a technician.
fork: the part of a bicycle frame that holds the front wheel
The mechanic replaced a bent fork on the old bicycle.
angled: positioned at a slant rather than straight
The mirror was angled so drivers could see around the sharp corner.
point: Mark the point where the two roads meet on the map.
where: It changes where the effort goes, away from the comfortable hours of reading.
tyre: a rubber covering fitted around the rim of a wheel

touches: present tense of touch, used with he/she/it; makes contact with
The front fork is angled, and the point where the tyre touches the ground sits behind the steering axis.
ground: the solid surface of the earth
Leaves covered the ground after the autumn winds.
sits: is located in a particular place
The old castle sits on a hill overlooking the valley.
behind: at or toward the back of something
She parked the car behind the old warehouse near the river.
line: a long thin mark or stroke
She drew a straight line across the page with a ruler.
axis: an imaginary line around which something turns or is arranged
The Earth spins on its axis once every twenty-four hours.
this: used to refer to a specific thing nearby or just mentioned
This is the best coffee I have had in years.
arrangement: a plan or agreement made in advance
They reached an arrangement to share the cost of repairs equally.
makes: A short walk after dinner makes falling asleep much easier.
into: moving towards the inside of something
She walked into the room and switched on the light.
automatically: without needing a person to operate it
The lights switch on automatically as soon as it gets dark.
without: not having; in the absence of
This arrangement lets the wheel turn into a lean without anyone touching the handlebars.
touching: the act of making physical contact with something
This arrangement makes the wheel turn into a lean automatically, without anyone touching the handlebars.
handlebars: the steering bar of a bicycle or motorcycle
He gripped the handlebars tightly as the bike sped downhill.
pushed: pressed against something to move it away

along: moving or extending in a continuous line on
Children were riding their bikes along the river path yesterday afternoon.
empty: The bus was almost empty at that late hour.
road: a wide path with a hard surface for vehicles
A new road now connects the two remote villages.
roll: to move by turning over and over, or move smoothly
The ball began to roll slowly down the gentle slope.
some: an unspecified amount or number of something
Could you buy some bread on your way home?
distance: the amount of space between two places or things
It's a short distance from here to the nearest train station.
before: earlier than a particular time or event
Please arrive at the airport before your flight is due to leave.
correcting: making something accurate by removing errors
The pilot spent several seconds correcting the aircraft's course after the gust.
badly: in a poor or unsatisfactory way
The team played badly in the first half of the match.
briefly: She paused briefly before continuing her speech to the crowd.
nobody: not a single person; no one
Nobody expected the small team to win the championship.
aboard: on or into a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle
All passengers were asked to come aboard before the ship departed.
you: used to refer to the person being spoken to
The method also feels worse while you are doing it.
test: a procedure used to check or examine something
She passed her driving test on the very first attempt.
any: used to refer to one or some of a thing, no matter which
Do you have any questions before we begin the meeting?
equipment: the tools or items needed for a particular purpose

push: to press against something to move it away
You need to push the heavy door hard to open it.
saddle: the seat on a bicycle, motorbike, or horse
He adjusted the saddle height before starting the ride.
let: to allow someone to do something
Her parents let her stay out late for the concert.
go: to move or travel from one place to another
We should go before the traffic gets worse.
run: to move quickly, or to continue moving under its own momentum
The car will run for a while even after the engine dies.
only: and no one or nothing more besides; just
Only a handful of tickets remained by the time we arrived.
slows: Heavy rain always slows the traffic on this road.
hold: keep or retain something, such as water or an object
These containers hold enough water for a week.
rigidly: in a stiff, strict, or unchanging way
The rules were applied rigidly, with no exceptions allowed.
straight: extending in one direction without a curve or bend
Draw a straight line from one corner to the other.
same: They wore the same colour shirts to the reunion.
topples: present tense of topple, used with he/she/it; falls over
Hold the handlebars rigidly straight and the same bicycle topples almost at once.
almost: very nearly but not completely or entirely
She almost missed the last train home after the concert ended.
at: used to show a specific place, time or point
We agreed to meet at the station at six o'clock.
once: immediately, without delay (used in the phrase 'at once')
The fire alarm made everyone leave the building at once.
source: the place or thing from which something originates

balance: a state in which different things are of equal weight or importance
Finding a balance between work and rest is not always easy.
who: used to ask about or refer to a person
The extra heat is dangerous for anyone who cannot afford to cool their home.
blocks: to stop something from passing or happening

destroys: damages something so badly it no longer exists
A single careless spark sometimes destroys an entire dry forest.
lesson: a period of teaching, or something learned from experience
The teacher planned an interactive lesson about the water cycle.
common: occurring often or found in many places; shared by many
Power cuts are common during the rainy season here.
in: expressing location inside or within something
The keys are in the top drawer of the desk.
engineering: the field of designing and building machines, structures, or systems
She studied engineering before moving into software design.
machine: a device with moving parts that performs a task
The factory installed a new machine to speed up packaging.
appears: becomes visible, or seems to be the case

be: to exist, or to have a particular state or quality

held: supported or kept in a position; past tense of hold

up: towards a higher place or position

grand: impressive in size, scale, or importance
The palace has a grand entrance hall with marble floors.
principle: a basic rule or belief that guides behaviour or reasoning

usually: A machine that appears to be held up by one principle is usually held up by several.
small: not large in size, amount, or degree
They live in a small apartment near the city center.
ones: particular items or people already mentioned or understood
The smaller phones sell better than the larger ones this year.
working: Understanding the pattern is the first step towards working around it.
together: with each other; combined into one group or place
Sourdough relies on wild yeasts and bacteria living together in a starter.
removing: the act of taking something away
Removing the old wallpaper took most of the weekend.
single: only one; not one of several

less: He eats less meat now than he used to.
damage: harm or injury caused to something, reducing its value or condition

expected: Removing any single support does less damage than expected.
